subproblems.title: C¹ cut-off of f near K to a compact perturbation of the identity supported in O (reused accepted declaration)
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P : ℕ) (O K : Set (Euclid P)) (f : Euclid P → Euclid P), IsOpen O → IsCompact K → K ⊆ O → ContDiffOn ℝ 1 f O → ∃ (φ : Euclid P → Euclid P) (V K' : Set (Euclid P)), IsOpen V ∧ K ⊆ V ∧ IsCompact K' ∧ K' ⊆ O ∧ ContDiff ℝ 1 φ ∧ (∀ x ∈ V, φ x = f x ∧ fderiv ℝ φ x = fderiv ℝ f x) ∧ ∀ x, x ∉ K' → φ x = x
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: steps 1–2 of the parent proof (Cutoff; Properties of φ). Two adaptations:
- The parent's open set V₀ = O ∩ U is written O here; the parent applies this lemma to O ∩ U.
- The smooth Urysohn cutoff is made explicit. The parent's K₁ is K' here and its W₀ is V.
This is also the audited proof of the comparator-accepted declaration dimred_mbl_pfb_c1_compact_perturbation (node root.dimension_reduction_results-a1.moving_blowups-a1.pushforward-a1.pf_boundary-a1.c1_perturbation-a1, candidate 0869ad75). Its frozen type is reused verbatim.

Notation.
- E := ℝ^P (Euclid P), a finite-dimensional, hence proper, real normed space.
- thickening r K := {z : infEdist(z, K) < r}; cthickening r K := {z : infEdist(z, K) ≤ r}.
- Df(x) := fderiv ℝ f x.

1. Margin. K is compact, O is open and K ⊆ O, so there is δ > 0 with cthickening δ K ⊆ O (Mathlib IsCompact.exists_cthickening_subset_open). Put:
 - s := thickening δ K, open (isOpen_thickening);
 - t := cthickening (δ/2) K, closed (isClosed_cthickening);
 - V := thickening (δ/2) K, open (isOpen_thickening).
 Then:
 - K ⊆ V (self_subset_thickening, since δ/2 > 0);
 - V ⊆ t (thickening_subset_cthickening);
 - t ⊆ s (cthickening_subset_thickening', since 0 < δ and δ/2 < δ).
 If K = ∅, all these sets are empty and the steps below go through unchanged.

2. Smooth cutoff (parent step 1). Apply the smooth Urysohn lemma in the finite-dimensional real space E (Mathlib exists_contDiff_support_eq_eq_one_iff, smoothness order ⊤ : ℕ∞) to the open set s and the closed set t ⊆ s. It gives χ : E → ℝ, C^∞, with values in [0, 1], support χ = s, and x ∈ t ⟺ χ(x) = 1. In particular χ is C¹ (ContDiff.of_le), and χ = 1 on V ⊆ t.

3. The compact set K' (the parent's K₁). Let K' := tsupport χ = closure(support χ) = closure s.
 - K' ⊆ cthickening δ K (closure_thickening_subset_cthickening), and cthickening δ K ⊆ O by step 1.
 - K' is closed (isClosed_tsupport) and lies in the compact set cthickening δ K (IsCompact.cthickening, E proper), so K' is compact (IsCompact.of_isClosed_subset).

4. Definition (parent step 1). For x ∈ E put φ(x) := χ(x)·f(x) + (1 − χ(x))·x. No regularity of f off O is used.

5. φ = id off K' (parent step 2(b)). If x ∉ K' = tsupport χ, then χ(x) = 0 (image_eq_zero_of_notMem_tsupport). So φ(x) = 0·f(x) + 1·x = x.

6. φ = f near K (parent step 2(c)). Let x ∈ V. V is open, so it is a neighbourhood of x. Every y ∈ V lies in t, so χ(y) = 1 and φ(y) = 1·f(y) + 0·y = f(y). Thus φ and f agree on a neighbourhood of x (φ =ᶠ[𝓝 x] f). This gives:
 - φ(x) = f(x) (Filter.EventuallyEq.eq_of_nhds);
 - Dφ(x) = Df(x) (Filter.EventuallyEq.fderiv_eq: the Fréchet derivative at x depends only on the germ at x).

7. φ is C¹ on E (parent step 2(a)). By contDiff_iff_contDiffAt it suffices to show ContDiffAt ℝ 1 φ x for every x ∈ E. Since K' ⊆ O, E = O ∪ (E ∖ K'), so the two cases below cover E.
 (a) x ∈ O. O is open, so O ∈ 𝓝 x and f is C¹ at x (ContDiffOn.contDiffAt). χ is C¹ at x by step 2, and the constant 1 and the identity are C¹. A real C¹ function times a vector-valued C¹ map is C¹ at x, and so are sums and differences of C¹ maps (ContDiffAt.smul, ContDiffAt.add, ContDiffAt.sub). Hence φ = χ·f + (1 − χ)·id is C¹ at x.
 (b) x ∉ O. Then x ∉ K', because K' ⊆ O (step 3). The complement of the closed set K' is an open neighbourhood of x on which φ = id (step 5). So φ =ᶠ[𝓝 x] id, and φ is C¹ at x (ContDiffAt.congr_of_eventuallyEq with contDiffAt_id).

8. Conclusion. The triple (φ, V, K') has all required properties:
 - V is open and K ⊆ V (step 1);
 - K' is compact and K' ⊆ O (step 3);
 - φ is C¹ on E (step 7);
 - φ(x) = f(x) and Dφ(x) = Df(x) for every x ∈ V (step 6);
 - φ(x) = x for every x ∉ K' (step 5). ∎
proof_key_steps: Choose δ > 0 with cthickening δ K ⊆ O. V := thickening (δ/2) K is an open neighbourhood of K, and V ⊆ t := cthickening (δ/2) K ⊆ s := thickening δ K.
Smooth Urysohn (exists_contDiff_support_eq_eq_one_iff) gives χ ∈ C^∞(E, [0,1]) with support χ = s and χ = 1 exactly on t. K' := tsupport χ ⊆ cthickening δ K ⊆ O is compact.
φ := χ·f + (1 − χ)·id equals id off K' and equals f on the open set V, so φ = f and Dφ = Df on V (EventuallyEq.fderiv_eq).
φ is C¹ at points of O (a C¹ combination of χ, f and id) and at points off O (φ = id near them, since K' ⊆ O), so ContDiff ℝ 1 φ.

subproblems.title: Simon 6.2.24(1) for a C¹ compact perturbation of the identity: ∂T = 0 implies ∂S = 0 (reused accepted declaration)
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (U K : Set (Euclid P)) (T S : GeometricCurrentOn U n) (R : IMRep U n) (φ : Euclid P → Euclid P), IsOpen U → R.Represents T → IsCompact K → K ⊆ U → ContDiff ℝ 1 φ → (∀ x, x ∉ K → φ x = x) → (∀ ω : TestFormOn U n, S ω = ∫ x in R.carrier, (R.mult x : ℝ) * R.orient x (((ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) n) (φ x)).compContinuousLinearMap (fderiv ℝ φ x)) ∂μHE[n]) → BoundaryVanishes T → BoundaryVanishes S
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: steps 0 and 3–7 of the parent proof: Simon Ch. 6, 2.24(1), ∂f_#T = f_#∂T (chapter-06.txt lines 413–415), extended from smooth to C¹ maps by smooth approximation.
- Here the statement is for a C¹ map φ equal to the identity off a compact K ⊆ U. In the parent, φ is the cut-off map and K is its compact set K₁; T, S are the parent's X, Q.
- This is the audited proof of the comparator-accepted declaration dpf_pushforward_formula_boundaryVanishes (node root.minimizing_implies_stationary-a1.diffeo_pushforward-a1.pushforward_boundary-a1, candidate 74a1c6be). Its frozen type is reused verbatim.
- Steps 2, 3 and 6 below are the accepted declarations dpf_smooth_approx_compact_perturbation, dpf_pb_smooth_pullback_isTestForm and dpf_pb_imrep_pullback_integral_tendsto. They are written out here so the argument is self-contained.

Notation.
- E := ℝ^P; M := R.carrier, θ := R.mult, ξ := R.orient; Hⁿ := μHE[n]; μ := Hⁿ⌞M.
- λ := Lebesgue measure on E, and ∗ is convolution with respect to λ; I := identity of E.
- For a C¹ map ψ and a p-form β, ψ^#β(x) := β(ψ(x))∘Dψ(x) = (β (ψ x)).compContinuousLinearMap (fderiv ℝ ψ x).
- d := exteriorDerivative = extDeriv.

1. Reduction (parent step 0). If n = 0, BoundaryVanishes S is True by definition. Let n = m + 1 and assume T.boundary = 0.
 - By extensionality of currents (GeometricCurrentOn.ext), it suffices to prove S.boundary(η) = 0 for every η ∈ 𝒟^m(U).
 - By GeometricCurrentOn.boundary_apply, S.boundary(η) = S(dη), where dη is the test form exteriorDerivativeTestOn U m η ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U). Likewise T(dη') = T.boundary(η') = 0 for every η' ∈ 𝒟^m(U).
 - Fix η ∈ 𝒟^m(U) and put α := dη. It is a C^∞ n-form with tsupport α ⊆ tsupport η, a compact subset of U (exteriorDerivative_isTestForm, tsupport_exteriorDerivative_subset). So α is continuous with compact support and ‖α‖_∞ := sup_y ‖α(y)‖ < ∞.

2. Smooth approximation (parent step 3). Claim: there are C^∞ maps ψ_k : E → E (k ∈ ℕ), a compact K' ⊆ U and a constant C such that:
 - ψ_k(x) = x for x ∉ K';
 - ‖Dψ_k(x)‖ ≤ C for all k and x (so C ≥ 0);
 - ψ_k(x) → φ(x) and Dψ_k(x) → Dφ(x) for every x.
 Proof:
 (a) Margin. K is compact, U is open and K ⊆ U, so there is δ > 0 with K' := cthickening δ K = {x : infEdist(x, K) ≤ δ} ⊆ U (IsCompact.exists_cthickening_subset_open). K' is compact (IsCompact.cthickening, E proper).
 (b) Perturbation. g := φ − I is C¹, and g(x) = 0 for x ∉ K. So support g ⊆ K and, K being closed, tsupport g ⊆ K: g has compact support. On the open set E ∖ K we have φ = I, so Dφ = I there (Filter.EventuallyEq.fderiv_eq), i.e. Dg = Dφ − I vanishes off K. Dg is continuous with support in the compact K, hence A := sup_x ‖Dg(x)‖ < ∞.
 (c) Mollifiers. For k ∈ ℕ let β_k : ContDiffBump (0 : E) have rIn = δ/(2(k+1)) < rOut = δ/(k+1), and put ρ_k := β_k.normed λ. Then:
 - ρ_k is C^∞ and ρ_k ≥ 0 (ContDiffBump.nonneg_normed);
 - ∫ρ_k dλ = 1 (ContDiffBump.integral_normed);
 - ρ_k(t) = 0 whenever |t| ≥ δ/(k+1).
 Define ψ_k := I + ρ_k ∗ g, i.e. ψ_k(x) = x + ∫ρ_k(t) g(x − t) dλ(t).
 (d) Smoothness. ρ_k is C^∞ with compact support, and g is continuous, hence locally integrable. So ρ_k ∗ g is C^∞ (HasCompactSupport.contDiff_convolution_left with n = ⊤ : ℕ∞), and so is ψ_k.
 (e) ψ_k = I off K'. Let x ∉ K'. If ρ_k(t) ≠ 0 then |t| < δ/(k+1) ≤ δ. Then x − t ∉ K: otherwise infEdist(x, K) ≤ |t| < δ and x ∈ K'. So g(x − t) = 0 whenever ρ_k(t) ≠ 0. Hence (ρ_k ∗ g)(x) = 0 and ψ_k(x) = x, for every k.
 (f) Derivative bound. g is C¹ with compact support and ρ_k is locally integrable, so D(ρ_k ∗ g)(x) = ∫ρ_k(t) Dg(x − t) dλ(t) (HasCompactSupport.hasFDerivAt_convolution_right). Hence Dψ_k(x) = I + ∫ρ_k(t) Dg(x − t) dt. Using ρ_k ≥ 0, ∫ρ_k = 1 and ‖I‖ ≤ 1: ‖Dψ_k(x)‖ ≤ 1 + ∫ρ_k(t)‖Dg(x − t)‖ dt ≤ 1 + A =: C.
 (g) Pointwise convergence. Fix x. rOut(β_k) = δ/(k+1) → 0, and g and Dg are continuous. So (ρ_k ∗ g)(x) → g(x) and (ρ_k ∗ Dg)(x) → Dg(x) (ContDiffBump.convolution_tendsto_right_of_continuous). Hence ψ_k(x) → x + g(x) = φ(x) and Dψ_k(x) → I + Dg(x) = Dφ(x).
 For P = 0 the claim is trivial: E is a point, g = 0 and ψ_k = I = φ.

3. Pulled-back test forms (parent step 4). Fix k and β ∈ {η, α}; β is C^∞ with compact support in U.
 - Smoothness: ψ_k^#β(x) = (compContinuousLinearMapCLM (Dψ_k(x)))(β(ψ_k(x))).
 - x ↦ β(ψ_k(x)) is C^∞ (ContDiff.comp), and x ↦ Dψ_k(x) is C^∞ because ψ_k is C^∞.
 - L ↦ compContinuousLinearMapCLM L is analytic on all of End(E) (ContinuousAlternatingMap.analyticOnNhd_compContinuousLinearMapCLM), hence C^∞.
 - Applying a C^∞ family of continuous linear maps to a C^∞ family of vectors is C^∞ (ContDiff.clm_apply). So ψ_k^#β is C^∞.
 - Support: F := tsupport β ∪ K' is a compact subset of U. If x ∉ F, the open set W := E ∖ F is a neighbourhood of x on which ψ_k = I. So Dψ_k = I on W, and ψ_k^#β(z) = β(z) = 0 for z ∈ W. Hence ψ_k^#β vanishes on the open set E ∖ F, so tsupport(ψ_k^#β) ⊆ F ⊆ U and ψ_k^#β has compact support.
 Therefore ψ_k^#η ∈ 𝒟^m(U) and ψ_k^#α ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U).

4. Naturality of d (parent step 5). d(ψ_k^#η) = ψ_k^#(dη) = ψ_k^#α pointwise on E. This is Mathlib extDeriv_pullback, or SimonGMT exteriorDerivativeOn_pullbackFormWithin on univ. It applies at every x because η is C^∞, hence differentiable at ψ_k(x), and ψ_k is C^∞, in particular C². So the test form exteriorDerivativeTestOn U m (ψ_k^#η) equals the test form ψ_k^#α (same underlying form).

5. The approximating values vanish (parent step 6). T.boundary = 0 and R represents T. For every k:
 0 = T.boundary(ψ_k^#η) = T(d(ψ_k^#η)) = T(ψ_k^#α) = ∫_M θ(x)·ξ(x)(α(ψ_k(x))∘Dψ_k(x)) dHⁿ(x) =: I_k.

6. Passage to the limit (parent step 7). Put h_k(x) := θ(x)·ξ(x)(α(ψ_k(x))∘Dψ_k(x)) and h(x) := θ(x)·ξ(x)(α(φ(x))∘Dφ(x)).
 (a) Measurability. θ is measurable and ξ is μ-a.e. strongly measurable (R.aestronglyMeasurable_orient). The covector fields x ↦ α(ψ_k(x))∘Dψ_k(x) and x ↦ α(φ(x))∘Dφ(x) are continuous: α, ψ_k, φ, Dψ_k and Dφ are continuous, and (γ, L) ↦ γ∘L is jointly continuous (ContinuousAlternatingMap.continuous_compContinuousLinearMapCLM). Evaluation (ξ, γ) ↦ ξ(γ) is continuous bilinear. So each h_k and h is μ-a.e. strongly measurable.
 (b) Pointwise convergence. Fix x: ψ_k(x) → φ(x) and α is continuous; Dψ_k(x) → Dφ(x); composition is jointly continuous; and ξ(x) is continuous linear. So h_k(x) → h(x).
 (c) Domination.
 - By R.orients, for μ-a.e. x there is an orthonormal τ with ξ(x)(γ) = ±γ(τ₁, …, τₙ) for all γ. Hence |ξ(x)(γ)| ≤ ‖γ‖·∏‖τ_i‖ = ‖γ‖ (ContinuousAlternatingMap.le_opNorm).
 - Put C₀ := tsupport α ∪ K', a compact subset of U. If h_k(x) ≠ 0, then α(ψ_k(x)) ≠ 0, so ψ_k(x) ∈ tsupport α. If moreover x ∉ K', then x = ψ_k(x). So h_k(x) ≠ 0 implies x ∈ C₀.
 - Since ‖γ∘L‖ ≤ ‖γ‖‖L‖ⁿ (ContinuousAlternatingMap.norm_compContinuousLinearMap_le), |h_k(x)| ≤ Cⁿ·‖α‖_∞·θ(x)·1_{C₀}(x) for μ-a.e. x and every k.
 - This bound is measurable and μ-integrable, since ∫_{M∩C₀} θ dHⁿ < ∞ (R.locallyIntegrable_mult, C₀ compact ⊆ U).
 By the dominated convergence theorem (MeasureTheory.tendsto_integral_of_dominated_convergence), I_k → ∫_M h dHⁿ.

7. Conclusion. Apply the hypothesis on S to the test form dη = exteriorDerivativeTestOn U m η, whose underlying form is α:
 S.boundary(η) = S(dη) = ∫_M h dHⁿ = lim_k I_k = 0,
 by step 6 and uniqueness of limits, since I_k = 0 for all k (step 5). As η ∈ 𝒟^m(U) was arbitrary, S.boundary = 0, i.e. BoundaryVanishes S. ∎
proof_key_steps: n = 0 is trivial. For n = m + 1 it suffices that S(dη) = 0 for every η ∈ 𝒟^m(U) (GeometricCurrentOn.ext, boundary_apply).
Mollify g = φ − id: ψ_k := id + ρ_k ∗ g is C^∞ and equals id off the compact K' = cthickening δ K ⊆ U. Also ‖Dψ_k‖ ≤ 1 + sup‖Dg‖, and ψ_k → φ, Dψ_k → Dφ pointwise.
ψ_k^#η and ψ_k^#(dη) are test forms in U, supported in tsupport η ∪ K'. Since d(ψ_k^#η) = ψ_k^#(dη) (extDeriv_pullback), ∂T = 0 gives 0 = ∫_M θξ(dη(ψ_k x)∘Dψ_k(x)) dHⁿ.
Dominated convergence with bound Cⁿ‖dη‖_∞θ1_{tsupport dη ∪ K'} gives S(dη) = lim = 0, i.e. BoundaryVanishes S.
